children: Navitas Semiconductor shares rose after the company launched its latest power-delivery board to support Nvidia's power architectures for AI data centers.
The stock gained 6% to $10.58 in after-hours trading Monday, after falling more than 7% during the regular session. Through the close, shares were up 40% this year.
The new 24-kilowatt board extends Navitas' portfolio of 800 AI data-center platforms, building on the previously announced 20-kilowatt board developed with Nvidia.

The board was designed in Nvidia's latest form factor and can be integrated into the compute motherboard as close as possible to XPUs, minimizing power-delivery losses and supporting high-power demands.
It also has a simplified power architecture that improves system efficiency and reliability while reducing power losses, board space and overall power-delivery complexity.
